text:
Soojin Lee: Design review ask for Standard Demo v1 deck. We’re close on narrative but slides are still feeling “busy” + screenshots are inconsistent. Can folks drop feedback on visual hierarchy / diagrams / screenshot standards? Current working deck: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1redwood-demo-deck-working (slides 6–18 are the worst offenders) :eyes:

Camila Reyes: :eyes: Took a first pass. Overall story is strong, but design needs to make the *differentiators* pop faster.
- Visual hierarchy: we have too many slides where headline, subhead, bullets, and screenshot all fight for attention. Pick 1 hero element per slide.
- Headlines should be “claim + outcome” not feature inventory. e.g. “Predictable latency under load” vs “Continuous batching”.
- The green + red accents are currently used for everything. Reserve one accent color for “proof” (charts/metrics) and one for “control” (policy toggles).
- Lots of 11–12pt body copy. Can we cut 30–40% of text and move details to speaker notes?

Talia Benson: +1 on cutting copy. Also: we have a few diagram slides that are doing too much (hosted/dedicated/private all in one spaghetti). Suggest split:
1) “One API” diagram (simple)
2) “Deployment modes” (3 columns)
3) “Control plane + routing” (only for technical branch)
If we keep all in one, it’s not demo-friendly.

Markus Klein: Agree. From SE POV, the messy diagrams make it harder to talk while driving the console. The best slides are the ones with a single screenshot + 2 callouts.
Specific: slide “Routing + fallback” diagram currently has ~12 arrows. If we simplify to:
Request -> Policy -> Primary route -> (if failure/latency) fallback route
…and then show the actual rule in Console, it’ll land.

Renee Sullivan: Screenshot standards suggestion (so we don’t redo this every time):
- Always 16:9 crop, no browser chrome unless needed for credibility.
- Use the same region + tenant name in every screenshot. (Right now I see 3 different nav configs.)
- Dark mode vs light mode: pick one and stick with it. I vote light for print/PDF readability.
- Redactions: ensure no real customer orgs or API keys. Replace with DEMO-TENANT + dummy IDs.
- Use callout style consistently (same radius, same shadow). No mixed circles/arrows.

Camila Reyes: Yes to standards. Also: screenshot quality is currently uneven (some are slightly blurry). Please ensure all are direct captures from the app (not zoomed-in snips from a low-res image).
Rule of thumb: if you can’t read the primary table headers at 100% in Slides, it’s not shippable.

Soojin Lee: This is helpful. Re: hierarchy — would you rather we do more “big claim” slides, then “proof slide” (metric/dashboard) after? Or combine claim + proof on one?

Camila Reyes: For this deck, combine where possible. But only if it stays clean.
Pattern:
- Left: 1 sentence claim + 2 bullets max
- Right: proof (screenshot/graph)
- Footer: tiny “what’s happening” label (e.g. “Load test + automatic fallback”) so it’s skimmable.
If a slide needs more than 2 bullets, it probably needs to be two slides.

Isabelle Laurent: Jumping in with enablement hat: we should standardize where “persona branches” live visually.
Right now “If you’re security…” is buried in notes. Can we add a small tag in the corner like:
- PLATFORM PATH
- ML PATH
- SECURITY PATH
So AEs don’t miss the branch in live demos.

Markus Klein: +1. Also would help if the deck has “driver cues” that don’t show to prospects (presenter view only). Like “CLICK: Console > Routes > Policy”.

Soojin Lee: We can add those as speaker notes + a tiny icon marker for internal PDF. For customer-facing export we can hide the marker.

Renee Sullivan: On diagram simplification, I can take first stab rewriting the “Unified runtime” slide. Current diagram shows 7 boxes. We can reduce to 3:
API -> Runtime -> Observability
Then “deployment modes” as separate row below.

Camila Reyes: Another design note: typography. Please don’t mix 3 different code fonts in snippets. Pick one monospace and keep it.
And code snippets should be *short* (3–8 lines). Any longer belongs in appendix / quickstart.

Talia Benson: Flagging slide 12 (cost controls). It has a dashboard screenshot + 5 callouts + a paragraph. Maybe make it:
- Slide A: “Token-level cost visibility” with a single dashboard
- Slide B: “Controls to reduce unit cost” with 3 toggles (batching/caching/quant)

Soojin Lee: Yep. That’s consistent with narrative.
Question: for “benchmark proof points” slide, we’ve been avoiding hard numbers. Design currently shows a big chart with numbers. Should we swap to ranges / “typical improvement” language?

Camila Reyes: Keep numbers out of the main flow. We can say “measured improvements” + show relative bars (index to baseline = 1.0) without absolute ms/$.
If asked, the SE can reference “acceptable ranges” doc verbally. We do not want a screenshot of a spreadsheet floating around.

Markus Klein: +100. Prospects will screenshot and then hold us to it regardless of workload. Relative is safer.

Isabelle Laurent: Also from sales ops side: if we remove numbers, we should add a slide footer disclaimer once: “Performance varies by model/hardware/sequence length; we’ll validate in your environment.”

Renee Sullivan: Screenshot detail: please make sure tenant name is consistent.
Recommendation: “Redwood Demo (Standard)” as org name, and route names like:
- demo.chat.streaming
- demo.tool.calling
- demo.fallback.primary
Makes it easier to follow talk track + console clickpath.

Soojin Lee: Love the route naming convention.
Action items I’m capturing:
1) Reduce text density (max 2 bullets) + move detail to notes
2) Split deployment modes diagram into simpler slides
3) Routing/fallback diagram: simplify to 4-step flow + show policy in Console
4) Lock screenshot standards (16:9, light mode, no blur, consistent tenant/region, consistent callouts)
5) Persona branch tags on relevant slides
6) Benchmark slide: relative/indexed, no absolute numbers
I’ll update deck v0.9 by Friday and re-request a quick final pass.

Camila Reyes: Sounds good. If you want, I can do a 15 min async Loom after you update v0.9 and call out any remaining “too busy” slides.

Talia Benson: :thumbsup: Please also drop the screenshot standards in the shared folder as a one-pager so we can enforce during future edits.

Soojin Lee: Will do. I’ll draft a “Console screenshot style guide” and pin it in this channel.

Markus Klein: Thank you. This will save us from SE heroics. :pray:

Renee Sullivan: When you have v0.9, tag me and I’ll sanity check the clickpath matches the talk track.

Camila Reyes: +1 and please make sure we’re not showing any “internal only” toggles that don’t exist on customer tenants (I saw one in slide 15).

Soojin Lee: Oof good catch — I think that was from staging. Will replace with demo tenant capture.

Isabelle Laurent: One last thought: for security persona, can we make the “Private/VPC” slide more readable (less product UI, more “controls” list)? Current screenshot is hard to parse fast.

Soojin Lee: Yep, we’ll convert that to an icon-based controls grid + only 1 small screenshot for audit logs.

Camila Reyes: Perfect. Keep it simple + credible.

Soojin Lee: Thanks all. Closing loop here and I’ll repost v0.9 link Friday.
